content.comment_body: I tried to open my [product_name] network project, but an 'Unknown Error' appears when I attempt to access it. It was working fine yesterday. This has happened before, and last time I had to rebuild the entire program, which I want to avoid. I read on the forum that you might be able to recover a .lsc file from a .lnp archive. How is that done? Also, can anyone explain why these projects become corrupted unexpectedly?
Could you please upload your network project in a ZIP archive?
That worked, thanks a lot! Could you explain your method so I can use it next time?

The .lnp file is actually an archive. I used WinRAR to extract its contents. Inside, there is the file "[document].xml" and a folder named "[article_no]". The "[document].lsc" file is located within this folder. Open [product_name], go to the "Network Project" section, and in the network view, right-click for the context menu and select "Import". Then, choose the "[document].lsc" file in your file explorer. This will import the diagram. Finally, save your network project again.
Thank you very much for your assistance!

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience unexpected error messages like 'Unknown Error' when attempting to open previously working network projects in [product_name]. The issue recurs and can lead to project corruption and data loss. Recovery can be achieved by manually extracting and importing files from an archive, which demonstrates concerns about project stability and the reliability of the recovery process.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable handling of project files without unexpected corruption, clear and informative error messages, and simple built-in recovery features in the software.
